note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a STV 12, Schedule 2; A06b STV 12, Schedule 2; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 7 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: No provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship), A02a (birth in country: Generally applicable provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory unconditionally; by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states (the dataset codes no separate descent rule for a child born in the country, birth there giving it; the parent's sex is read from mode A01b). Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Frequently Asked Questions, Office of the Prime Minister, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (the office that processes citizenship applications). It confirmed the years of residence, descent and the limit abroad. It was silent on renunciation, loss on taking another citizenship and birth in the territory, which still rest on the sources above, re-read that day and found the same. The office calls the seven-year route registration; a Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2023 is listed by the Assembly and wasn't read.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in St Vincent for 12 months immediately prior to the application, and was either resident in St Vincent, or in government service for 6 out of 9 years predating the 12-month period. ... Renunciation of another citizenship required (at the discretion of the Minister). ... n.a. ... No provision ... Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship ... Person is born abroad to a citizen otherwise than by descent. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in St Vincent. Unless born to a foreign diplomat and neither parent is a citizen, or one of the parents is an enemy alien and child is born in a place then under occupation by the enemy. Citizenship Act declares that the mother, specifically, must be a citizen. ... No provision

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions, Office of the Prime Minister, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (the office that processes citizenship applications)
sources.said: citizenship? i. By Registration - (a) by marriage to a Vincentian (b) by having temporary residence for seven (7) or more consecutive years, or (c) by having permanent residence status. ii. By Descent - If one (1) or both parents was/were born in St. Vincent and the Grenadines. 2. Can children who are born abroad to parents who are Vincentian citizens by descent apply for citizenship? Only if they have been granted temporary/permanent residence in the State which meets the criteria for the granting of citizenship by registration.

atBirth.descentAbroad: Person is born abroad to a citizen otherwise than by descent.
